name: Image
summary: Present a native image with Mux styling and bounded source recovery.

useWhen: Presenting an image while preserving native image dimensions, loading, and events.
Showing a photo, screenshot, diagram, or illustration in a box with a declared width and height.
avoidWhen: Cropping, editing, or processing image content.
Showing a compact picture of a person or workspace; use Avatar.
Opening a larger view of a picture; use Lightbox.

obligations: Supply a meaningful alt string for informative images; use alt="" for decorative images.
Preserve native image dimensions, source-set selection, refs, and load/error events.
When a fallback source is supplied, retry it once after the primary source fails and reset recovery when src or srcSet changes.

behavior: Renders a native HTMLImageElement and forwards native attributes, dimensions, refs, and callbacks.
When the primary source fails to load and fallbackSrc or fallbackSrcSet is supplied, the image switches to the fallback once and sets data-fallback.
If the fallback also fails, or none is supplied, the image sets data-error, keeps the failed source, and tries nothing further.
Changing src, srcSet, fallbackSrc, or fallbackSrcSet starts recovery over, so the new primary source is tried first.
onError runs for every load error, including the failure of the fallback.
radius and fit select the muxui-image--radius-* and muxui-image--fit-* modifier classes without changing intrinsic image dimensions.
When width and height are both set, the declared box keeps its ratio through the --muxui-image-ratio custom property, so fit applies and loading does not shift layout.
Consumer classes and styles can override --muxui-image-ratio.
accessibility: alt is required by the public type and runtime contract; an empty alt keeps decorative images out of the accessibility tree.
The native image remains the accessible host and no loading animation is introduced.

requirements.reason: Native dynamic colors do not apply to the React web binding.
Native font metrics do not apply to the React web binding.
